config.title: useRef Typing

intro.title: useRef Typing
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple typing speed test application where you can start a timer and track your keystrokes. You'll learn how to use the useRef hook in React to directly access and manipulate DOM elements, like an input field, without causing re-renders. The core concept is using useRef with TypeScript to create a typed reference for DOM elements, ensuring type safety. You'll work with React, TypeScript, and JSX to handle events and update the UI based on user input.
intro.usecase: In real applications, useRef typing is essential for managing DOM elements in interactive UI components. For example, in dashboard applications with real-time charts, developers use typed refs to access canvas elements for drawing animations and handling resize events. Form builders use typed refs to focus specific input fields programmatically when validation errors occur. In complex navigation menus, typed refs help manage focus states between dropdown items for accessibility compliance. This pattern ensures type safety when directly interacting with HTML elements while maintaining React's declarative approach.

objectives: Initialize a typed useRef hook with a specific DOM element type
Apply TypeScript generics to define the reference target type
Bind the typed useRef instance to a JSX element via the ref attribute
Manipulate DOM properties safely using the typed current property
Configure a useRef to store mutable values with explicit type annotations
Control component behavior by integrating typed refs with event handlers
Construct a React component that utilizes typed references for form inputs

steps.title: Import React and useRef
steps.instruction: Import React and the useRef hook from the 'react' library.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useRef from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useRef hook are available for use in the component.
successCriteria: React and useRef are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useRef, making them available for use in your component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure you're importing both React and useRef from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import both React and useRef from the 'react' library.

steps.title: Create main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named TypingApp that returns JSX. The component should return a simple <div> element for now.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function with the name TypingApp. Inside, return a <div> element.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useRef } from 'react';

// Create the TypingApp component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named TypingApp is defined, returning a <div> element.
successCriteria: The TypingApp component is defined and returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the TypingApp component. This will be the main container for our typing demonstration.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the component, but make sure it's named exactly 'TypingApp' and returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named TypingApp that returns a <div> element.

steps.title: Initialize useRef for input element
steps.instruction: Inside your TypingApp component, declare a ref using useRef() and assign it to a variable named inputRef.
steps.hint: Call useRef() and store the result in a variable. The initial value can be null since we'll attach it to a DOM element later.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a ref for a DOM element
const inputRef = useRef(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a ref variable ready to be attached to an input element in a later step.
successCriteria: A variable named inputRef is declared using useRef(null) inside the component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a ref that can be attached to an input element.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useRef() and storing the result in a variable named inputRef.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to declare a ref variable using useRef() inside the component.

steps.title: Initialize state for text input
steps.instruction: Inside the TypingApp component, import and use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'inputText' with an initial value of an empty string.
steps.hint: You'll need to import useState from 'react' and call it inside your component to create the state variable.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'inputText' initialized to an empty string, ready to store the user's typed input.
successCriteria: useState is imported from 'react' and used to create an 'inputText' state variable with initial value ''
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the inputText state variable. This will allow us to track what the user types in the input field.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've imported useState from 'react' and created a state variable named 'inputText' with an initial value of an empty string.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to import useState from 'react' and use it inside the TypingApp component to create a state variable named 'inputText' with an initial value of ''.

steps.title: Create focus handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the TypingApp component, create a function named handleFocus that calls the focus() method on the ref's current property.
steps.hint: Define a function that accesses the ref's current property and calls focus() on it.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleFocus function is defined inside the component, ready to focus the input element when called.
successCriteria: The handleFocus function is defined and calls focus() on the ref's current property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the focus handler function that will allow you to programmatically focus the input element.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it calls focus() on the ref's current property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Create a function named handleFocus that calls focus() on the ref's current property.

steps.title: Create input change handler
steps.instruction: Inside the TypingApp component, create a function named handleInputChange that takes an event parameter and updates the text state with the input's current value.
steps.hint: Define a function that receives an event object and calls setText with event.target.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named handleInputChange is defined inside the component, ready to update the text state when the input changes.
successCriteria: The handleInputChange function is defined, takes an event parameter, and calls setText with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the change handler that will update the text state as the user types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function takes an event parameter and updates the text state with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. It should be named handleInputChange and update the text state with the input's value.

steps.title: Add main container structure
steps.instruction: In your component's return statement, replace the null with a main div container that includes a heading and a paragraph.
steps.hint: Return JSX with a div containing an h1 and a p element. The heading can say something like 'Typing App' and the paragraph can introduce the app.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a basic JSX structure with a container div, heading, and paragraph.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a div with an h1 and a p element inside.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the basic structure for the app. The container div, heading, and paragraph are now in place.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have a div containing both an h1 and a p element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The return statement should be JSX with a div, heading, and paragraph. Try again.

steps.title: Add text input element with ref
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add an input element with its ref attribute connected to your useRef variable.
steps.hint: The ref attribute should point to the variable you created with useRef. This connects the DOM element to your ref.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: connecting a ref to an input
<input ref={myInputRef} />
steps.expectedOutcome: An input element appears in the component's structure with its ref properly connected to the useRef variable.
successCriteria: The input element has a ref attribute set to the useRef variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully connected the ref to an input element.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an input element, but make sure its ref attribute points to your useRef variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element is missing or the ref attribute isn't properly connected to your useRef variable.

steps.title: Wire input change handler and value
steps.instruction: Add the onChange handler and value prop to your existing input element to connect it to your state and change handler.
steps.hint: The input element should have both onChange and value attributes. onChange should call your change handler function, and value should be set to your state variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring an input
<input type="text" onChange={handleChange} value={inputValue} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The input element will be fully controlled by React, with its value synchronized to state and changes handled by your change handler function.
successCriteria: The input element has both onChange and value props correctly wired to the change handler and state variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully connected the input to React state and the change handler, making it a fully controlled component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added both the onChange and value props to the input element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element needs both onChange and value props to be properly controlled. Check that you're using your change handler function and state variable.

steps.title: Add focus button with click handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the return statement that calls your focus handler when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the onClick attribute on a button element to trigger your focus handler function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Button with click handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The app will have a button that, when clicked, focuses the input field using the ref.
successCriteria: A button element with onClick attribute calling the focus handler is added to the component's return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a button that uses the ref to focus the input field.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it has an onClick attribute that calls your focus handler function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't properly connected to the focus handler. Check that you've added onClick={yourFocusHandler} to the button.
